method:
Ryan had us introduce ourselves and also taught us the relevant theory. She asked us to observe a painting depicting a woman simultaneously filming various movies—a work rich in elements of both art and technology. To be honest, I didn't quite grasp it at first, but through our group discussion and Ryan’s explanations, I began to form my own understanding.
This week’s assignment is to write a reflection on what we saw. I can sense the interplay between art and technology and the mutual influence humans have on this relationship; while technology has become an integral part of the process, it is still humans who remain in control.

conclusion_future_work:
I get the impression that Ryan is familiar with a wide range of artists and artworks and is very knowledgeable. I’d like to set aside some time to have a proper conversation with him about my understanding of art and my final project; I’m sure he would offer very specific and constructive feedback.

Weekly Project:
I am deeply interested in both of these works:  In *Bicycle*, I observed how the voices of many individuals—recorded, and synthesized via computer technology—were pieced together to perform a song ." Clearly, creating this artwork required a vast number of distinct voices to be captured and combined digitally. Yet, I am that while it is increasingly common for machines or digital technologies to act as "artists," the results ultimately stem from human intervention. Could a machine ever create an artwork completely autonomously.This brings to mind the scene in the film . Although HAL is a computer, it speaks just like a human. As person begins to deactivate it, HAL’s voice slows down, and it starts to sing. The machine is aging just like a human being.I have come to realize that the technology employed in art needs to be controlled and balanced; otherwise, it could have negative effects. Technology can be part of art, and people can channel their emotions into technology to express art; clearly, the human element is inseparable from both art and technology.
results_discussion: I read several fascinating articles that introduced me to art across different eras and various forms of artistic expression. I was amazed, as much of this was entirely new to me; I was even surprised to discover that certain things I hadn't previously considered art actually fell into that category. Learning about the relationship between art and technology made me realize just how many wondrous things exist in this world. I also completed the reflection paper Ryan assigned; to be honest, I didn't quite grasp the material at first, but the fact that the same song—"Daisy Bell"—appeared in both readings piqued my curiosity. A quick Google search revealed that it was the first song ever created using a computer—a pioneering moment where art and technology converged in music! It was truly significant. I also noticed a fascinating contrast between the two articles: one focused on humans using technology to create music with a "machine-like" quality, while the other explored machines expressing human emotion. This reciprocal relationship sparked a great deal of inspiration for me.
